newsitem.title: USA: California can afford Calpers repayment-officials.
newsitem.headline: California can afford Calpers repayment-officials.

text.p: California's treasurer and finance director said on Wednesday the state has enough money in its accounts to immediately repay the state's largest pension fund $1.36 billion to settle a court judgment.
State Treasurer Matt Fong said there are "sufficient funds in the state treasury to make the transfer." Department of Finance Director Craig Brown agreed, saying "a sufficient appropriation exists."

The pronouncements cleared the way for state Controller Kathleen Connell to immediately repay the California Public Employees' Retirement System (Calpers) for money lawmakers improperly used to balance state budgets in the early 1990s.

A state appeals court ruled in February that the governor and the legislature improperly withheld the money from Calpers in the early 1990s to balance state budgets during California's deepest economic downturn since the Depression. In May, the state Supreme Court refused to rehear the case.
With more than $100 billion in assets, Calpers is the largest public pension system in the United States.
State lawmakers had hoped to pay the money back over several years. But Calpers was "unwilling to offer an affordable" repayment plan, Gov. Pete Wilson said.

Wilson said repaying Calpers $1.36 billion this year would require lawmakers to sharply curtail their spending plans. Funding for Wilson's tax cut proposals and money for other non-education programs could be eliminated, the governor said.
